Description: In the Attic, Victoria Maseko has a private conversation with Annie Beaumont. Annie apologizes for the earlier conflict and identifies Tony Dauer as the instigator. They then discuss Edmund Galley’s motives for inviting everyone, Victoria’s emotional confusion, and Annie’s reluctance to talk to Martha Galley about her own issues. Victoria also hands an item to Annie to hide on her behalf.
Location: Attic（Attic）
Key Information:
  - The Attic door is knocked again; the visitor is Victoria Maseko (No. 7), and Annie Beaumont (No. 2) opens the door to talk.
  - Annie apologizes and insists “it really wasn’t me,” then explicitly says “Tony Dauer did it,” and promises she won’t let Tony keep doing this.
  - Victoria denies the problem lies with Damian Maseko, saying she feels “something is strange—this isn’t right.”
  - They discuss Edmund Galley’s motives for inviting everyone: Victoria doesn’t understand why Edmund invited them and thinks he may be angry at her.
  - Annie points out the logical contradiction: if Edmund were truly angry, he wouldn’t have invited them; and Victoria doesn’t need to force herself to be his friend.
  - Victoria gives “some item” to Annie to hold; Annie agrees to hide it, but stresses she won’t keep it on her person.
  - Victoria says she handed it over to show goodwill and draw Edmund’s attention, and reflects that she might be mistaken.
  - In a sharper tone, Annie guesses Edmund invited Victoria to show off his relationship with Eve Dauer, and tells Victoria not to feel guilty.
  - Annie asks whether Victoria told “mom” (referring to Martha Galley, No. 5) about Annie’s situation; Victoria suggests Annie will eventually need to talk to Martha.
  - Annie proposes a conditional, provocative idea (having Victoria go clarify things with Edmund), but Victoria stops her and tells her not to cause trouble.
  - The conversation ends and the Attic door is closed.
Characters:
  [Annie Beaumont（Annie Beaumont）] Person No. 2.
    · Apologizes to Victoria and insists the earlier incident was not her doing.
    · Explicitly identifies Tony Dauer as the instigator and says she will stop him.
    · Agrees to hold and hide an item for Victoria, but stresses she will not keep it on her person.
    · Asks whether Victoria told Martha Galley about Annie’s issues, showing reluctance to communicate directly with Martha.
  [Victoria Maseko（Victoria）] Person No. 7.
    · Visits the Attic at night to privately talk with Annie.
    · Expresses unease about Edmund’s motives and her own situation, thinking Edmund may be unhappy with her for unknown reasons.
    · Hands an item to Annie to hold, trying to show goodwill and gain Edmund’s attention.
    · Tells Annie she will eventually need to talk things through with Martha, and stops Annie from causing further trouble.
